newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH MINE STRIKE MAY CAUSE POWER SHORTAGE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH MINE STRIKE MAY CAUSE POWER SHORTAGE.

text.p: A strike at Poland's state-owned lignite mine KWB Belchatow, which reduced coal deliveries to a giant nearby electical power plant, may cause a power shortage at the start of next week, the power plant said on Saturday.

Janusz Roswag, head engineer on duty at the Belchatow plant, which produces electicity for about 25 percent of the country, said output fell by two-thirds and may cause shortages when electrical power use increased on Monday.

"We are working on only four out of 12 power generating blocks with no power cuts expected over the week-end but as electical needs increase on Monday the situation could be difficult," Roswag told Reuters.
He said that other Polish power plants have activated reserves to cover any potential power shortages.
Roswag said the power plant's only coal supplier was KWB Belchatow but added that the mine's strikers guaranteed to deliver enough coal to operate the four blocks.
"To keep four blocks operational we must recieve 12,800 tonnes of coal within eight hours and so far the strikers have kept their promise to deliver the necessary amounts," he said.
On Friday workers at KWB Belchatow reduced coal deliveries in protest aimed at dismissing their director general after weeks of discussions yielded no results.

Late on Friday the Treasury Ministry said in a statement that it was seriously considering the charges against the director and said that strikers would be responsible for any possible losses caused by halting coal supplies.
